# LLM application engineering

Use when code calls a model API (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, local models).

## Prompts are code
- Keep prompts in versioned files or constants next to the code that uses them, with the variables clearly marked.
- Separate instructions from data. Put untrusted content (user input, web pages, documents, tool output) in clearly delimited sections and tell the model to treat it as data.
- Ask for structured output (JSON schema / tool calling) and validate it with a schema; retry or fail clearly on invalid output.

## Evals before shipping
- Build a small eval set of real inputs with expected properties (correct fields, refusal when appropriate, no leaked secrets).
- Run it on every prompt or model change and compare against the previous version. Track the pass rate, not vibes.

## Cost and latency
- Log tokens in and out per request. Set `max_tokens`. Use prompt caching for long stable prefixes where the provider supports it.
- Route easy tasks to smaller models and keep the big model for hard ones; measure quality on the eval set when you switch.
- Stream long responses, set timeouts, and retry only on retryable errors (429/5xx) with backoff.

## Safety
- The model's output is untrusted: never execute it, never render it as raw HTML, and validate any action it proposes against an allow-list.
- Tools the model can call must enforce the user's permissions server-side.
- Keep API keys on the server; never ship them to the browser or mobile apps.

## Verify
Unit tests with recorded responses or a stub client, the eval run, and a check that logs contain no prompts with personal data unless that is intended and disclosed.
